sentences.text:
This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of .75,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Sri.Manjunatha.N.M.,
S/o.Muninarayanappa, in a road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 10.07.2022 at about 07.30 p.m., the deceased Manjunatha.N.M was riding his Yamaha FZs Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-67-H-3822 towards Chintamani side from H cross and when he reached near Uratiagrahara Gate, on H-cross Chintamani Road, Kolar Taluk and District, a Goods Tempo bearing Regn.No.KA-53-D-0828,
driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against deceased's motor cycle.

Due to said accident, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter, he was shifted to MVJ Medical College Hospital, Hosakote, wherein he succumbed to the injuries during the course of treatment and spent a sum of .1,00,000/- towards treatment, medicine,
Conveyance, transportation and funeral and obsequies ceremonies.

Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and was working as a Field Representative (Medical Representative) for Maneesh Health Care (MHC), A Division of Maneesh Pharmaceuticals Ltd., Mumbai and he used to visit hospitals and clinics at Chikkaballapura, Kolar and Bengaluru Rural Districts for marketing purpose and was earning a sum of .25,000/- per month.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners lost the bread earning member of the family and put to lot of mental agony.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of tempo by its driver.
The respondent No.1 & 2, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
3. In pursuance of notice, both the respondent No.1 & 2 appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsel and filed their separate written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondents have denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondents have also denied age, occupation and income of deceased as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further the respondents have contended that the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further contended that the lorry belongs to first respondent and it has existing policy bearing Regn.No.0161983996 valid till 31.03.2023.

Further first respondent was shocked and surprised when the notice was received from the Vemgal Police Station stating the lorry was involved in the alleged accident took place near Uratiagrahara Gate, for which the first respondent visited the said police station.
The police have directed the 1st respondent to furnish photo copies of documents of vehicle, as per their directions this respondent furnished the documents and then they have released the vehicle.

Further contended that it had valid insurance coverage under the insurance policy bearing No.0161983996 valid till 31.03.2023 issued by second respondent and also the driver of vehicle belonging to 1 st respondent possessed valid driving license at the time of alleged accident.
The amount claimed by petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

5. Respondent No.2, in the written statement, contended that the goods vehicle was covered under the policy of insurance issued by respondent and the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and Muninarayanappa vs Suguna Foods Pvt Ltd on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58088335/

6. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that the son of petitioner namely Manjunatha N.M.,
succumbed to the injuries in the accident that took place on 10.07.2022 at about 07.30 p.m., near Uratiagrahara Gate, H.Cross, Chintamani Road, Kolar Taluk and District, when he was riding a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-67-H- 3822, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Goods Tempo bearing Regn.No.KA-53-D-0828 by its driver?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
4. What order or award?

7. In order to substantiate the contention of the petition, the Petitioner/father of deceased got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16 and closed his side of evidence.

On the other hand, the Assistant Professor of MVJ Medical College, Hoskote got examined as RW.1 and the respondent insurance company examined its Senior Manager as RW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 to 5 and closed their side of evidence.
8. Heard arguments on both side and perused the materials available on records.

9. This Tribunal answers the above issues as below:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.1:- It is the case of the petitioners that deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 10.07.2022 at about 07.30 p.m., near Uratiagrahara Gate, H. 11. The Petitioner/father of deceased Manjunatha.N.M examined as PW.1.

In the chief- examination,
PW.1 deposed that his son was riding his motor cycle and due to the rash and negligent driving of Goods tempo by its driver, the accident occurred.

In order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of goods tempo, the petitioners produced Ex.P1 First Information lodged by brother of deceased by name Sri.Nagaraj, S/o.Muninarayanappa with police on 11.07.2022 with respect to the accident occurred on 10.07.2022.
On the basis of first information lodged by said Nagaraj, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC and U/s.187 of M.V.Act.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of goods tempo by its driver.
The owner or driver of the offending does not appear to have challenged the FIR or its contents.
The petitioners furnished the mahazar and sketch which are marked as Ex.P.5 and P.8.
The said documents disclose the aspect of police visiting the spot of accident after registration of FIR.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to haven caused due to negligence on the part of driver of goods tempo.
The said document discloses negligence on the part of driver of goods tempo in the cause of accident.

The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to show that the facts, as shown in mahazar and sketch,
are contrary to the facts at the place of accident.
Ex.P.6 is the IMV Reports, wherein the damages caused to both the vehicles are mentioned.
Ex.P7 is the PM report, wherein deceased Sri.Manjunath.N.M is stated to have died due to head injury sustained.
Ex . P.9
- Inquest Report.
The said documents disclose the aspect of death of Manjunath.
12. The respondents specifically denied the involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.

The respondent No.2 specifically contended that there is no mention about registration number of the vehicle either in FIR or in medical records, which creates doubt about the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.
It is pertinent to note that in FIR as well as medical records, the occurring of accident is clearly mentioned.
In FIR, though the registration number is not mentioned, it is mentioned that the accident is caused due to negligence on the part of driver of canter.

The respondent No.2 summoned Assistant Professor of MVG Medical College,
Hosakote and got examined witness as RW.2.
RW.2 furnished MLC and police intimation which are marked as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3.
On perusal of Ex.R.1, MLC Register Extract, the history is mentioned as road traffic accident between two wheeler and four wheeler occurred near H-Cross Market.
The place and the time of accident mentioned in Ex.R.1 is similar to the contents of FIR and contention of petitioner.
Though Ex.R1 does not disclose the registration number of the vehicle, it is clearly mentioned that the accident took place between two wheeler and four wheeler.

Further, in Ex.R.3,
police intimation, also there is mention about occurring of accident near H-Cross Market.
Though the registration number is not mentioned in Ex.R1 to 3, the fact of accident between two wheeler and four wheeler could be noticed from the entries in the said documents.
During the cross examination, RW.1 stated that registration number will not be mentioned in MLC Extract.
The evidence of RW.1 and Ex.R1 to Ex.R3
does not appear to be sufficient and substantive to doubt the involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
13. Respondent No.1 is the owner of offending vehicle and he appeared before the tribunal through his counsel and filed the written statement.

Except filing the written statement, respondent No.1 not Muninarayanappa vs Suguna Foods Pvt Ltd on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58088335/
4 furnished any satisfactory materials to doubt or dispute the involvement of his vehicle in the accident.

sentences.text: Respondent No.1 not furnished any materials contrary to the documents furnished by petitioner.
Further, the petitioner furnished the IMV Report, which is marked as Ex.P.6.
Ex .P.6 discloses the aspect of damages caused to the offending vehicle as well as vehicle driven by deceased.
The offending vehicle is stated to have been damaged on the front right side edge of bumper.

Respondent No.1 not provided any proper explanation regarding the manner in which the damage,
as mentioned in Ex.P.6, was caused.
Respondent No.1 could have explained the manner of damage caused to the vehicle, in the objections filed by him.
But there is no explanation regarding the said aspect in the objections filed by respondent No.1.

Further, respondent No.1 could have examined the driver of offending vehicle in order to contradict/controvert the contention of petitioner regarding involvement of vehicle and negligence of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
But the driver of offending vehicle has not been examined before the tribunal by the respondents.
The IMV Report furnished before the tribunal clearly discloses the aspect of damages caused to the vehicle and no explanation is forthcoming regarding manner of damages caused to the vehicle.
The said aspect indicates involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
If the vehicle was not involved in the accident, then the respondent No.1 could have explained the manner of damage caused to the vehicle either to I.O or before the tribunal.
But respondent No.1 not provided any explanation in that regard in the objections filed by him.
The materials relied by the respondent No.2 are not sufficient and satisfactory in order to doubt or dispute the involvement of the offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The materials on record clearly disclose the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.

14. It is pertinent to note that in the objections filed by respondent No.1, it is stated that respondent No.1 got shocked and surprised when he received notice from the concerned police station stating the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
The said aspect indicates that respondent No.1 is aware about the filing of case against his vehicle.
Further, respondent No.1 could have stated before the I.O regarding non- involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
Respondent No.1 stated in the objection regarding the notice issued by I.O and getting the vehicle released by furnishing the documents.
On the said occasion, respondent No.1 could have stated that the vehicle was not involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of driver in the cause of accident.
But, the respondent No.1 does not appear to have stated anything about the non-involvement of the vehicle before the police.
The said aspect also indicates the involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Mere non-mentioning of registration number of the vehicle cannot be considered to be sufficient and satisfactory proof to doubt the involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondent No.2 contended that the offending vehicle has been implicated in the case.
But, no satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to substantiate the said contention.
The materials on record do not disclose the aspect of implicating the offending vehicle in the case.

15. Further, the I.O., after detailed investigation, filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 304(A) of IPC and U/s.187 of M.V.Act as per Ex.P.10.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending goods tempo.
In the final report, there is no mention about negligence on the part of driver of the Goods tempo.

The documents furnished by petitioners disclose the Muninarayanappa vs Suguna Foods Pvt Ltd on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58088335/
5 aspect of negligence on the part of driver of goods tempo in the cause of accident.

sentences.text: The respondents not placed any materials in order to rebut or disprove the documents furnished by the petitioners related to the aspect of negligence.
The owner or driver of the goods tempo does not appear to have challenged the FIR as well as final report filed by the police against the driver of offending vehicle.
The correctness of investigation does not appear to have been challenged by respondents in any manner.
In the cross examination of PW.1 also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited from the witness.
16. The respondents not placed sufficient and satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
The materials on record disclose the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The materials on record do not disclose the aspect of implication of offending vehicle in the case and not sufficient to substantiate the contention of respondents.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the documents furnished by the petitioners are to be looked into in order to ascertain the aspect of negligence.
The materials placed before the Tribunal points towards the negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
So, the oral and documentary evidence placed by the petitioners discloses that the accident was caused due to rash and negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of petitioners coupled with the documents produced before this tribunal, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Goods Tempo bearing Regn.No.KA-53-D-0828 by its driver and deceased succumbed to injuries.

Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like age, avocation, income of deceased, conveyance charges, funeral and obsequies, towards of loss of love and affection, etc.

(A) Towards dependency and loss of future earnings:
(i) In the petition, the age of the deceased Sri.Manjunatha.N.M. is shown as 29 years.
In order to prove age of deceased, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.12 & 13 - Notarized copy of Driving License and Aadhaar Card, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 21.11.1992.
The accident occurred on 10.07.2022.
As per the materials placed by the petitioners, the age of deceased appears to be 30 years as on the date of accident.
The respondents not furnished any materials to rebut or disprove the documents furnished by petitioners related to age of deceased.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the documents furnished by petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the age of deceased.
As per the materials, the age of the deceased is 30 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme court of India in Smt.Sarla Verma case the multiplier applicable in present case is '17'.
( ii )

The petitioners contended that deceased Mr.Manjunath was working as a Field Representative (Medical Representative) for Maneesh Health Care (MHC), A Division of Maneesh Pharmaceuticals Ltd., Mumbai and used to visit hospitals and clinics at Chikkaballapura, Kolar and Bengaluru Rural Districts for marketing Muninarayanappa vs Suguna Foods Pvt Ltd on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58088335/
6 purpose of the products of the above said company and he was earning a sum of .25,000/- per month.

sentences.text: In order to prove the occupation and income of deceased, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.11 - Pay slips.
In order to prove the same, he has not examined the author of said document.
The petitioners not made any efforts in order to examine the concerned persons from the company in order to substantiate the document furnished by them.
The petitioners not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to substantiate their contention related to occupation and income of the deceased.
The materials placed by the petitioners are not sufficient and satisfactory to show the occupation and income of the deceased.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional income is to be taken into consideration.
By considering the facts and circumstances of case, the notional income of deceased is considered as .15,500/- per month.
In Hem Raj V/s
the Oriental Insurance Company Ltd and others

the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that there cannot be distinction where there is positive evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guess work in the facts and circumstances of a case.
Both the situations stand at the same footing.
In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble supreme court of India, the petitioners are entitled for future prospects.

National Insurance Company Ltd V/s Pranaya Sethi and others case the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that, in case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40% of the established income should be warranted where the deceased was below 40 years.

sentences.text: In the case on hand deceased was aged about 30 years.
Hence, in view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioners are entitled for additional 40% to the established income.

The established income of the deceased was .15,500/- and 40% of .15,500/-
is .6,200/-.
So, the total gross income of deceased was .15,500/- + .6,200/- = .21,700/- per month.
As per the materials on record, deceased Sri.Manjunatha.N.M was a bachelor.
The petitioner, being the father of deceased, is considered as dependent.
Hence, this tribunal considered the petitioner was only dependent upon the income of deceased.

As per the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Dharwad Bench in MFA No.20759/2012 in case of Smt.Geeta V/s Smt.Sundarawwa and others wherein the Hon'ble High Court has held in its judgment at para N.8 as follows:
The arguments as regard the deduction towards personal expenses in the case of sole dependent is based on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 SCC 121.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that the deduction towards personal expenses should be 1/3rd when the dependents of the deceased are either two or three, 1/4th if the dependents are between 4 and 6 and 1/5th if the dependents are more than 6.

A coordinate bench of this Court has considered this question of deduction towards personal expenses if the deceased is survive by a sole dependent in the light of the decision in Sarla Verma's case referred supra and deducted 50%
towards personal expenses.

This court can only agree with the submissions by the learned counsel for the Insurer that the deduction towards personal expenses in the case of a sole dependent should be 50% (or 1/2) of the Income as it stands to reason that if the permissible deduction in the case the number of dependents is either 2 or 3 Muninarayanappa vs Suguna Foods Pvt Ltd on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58088335/
7 should be 1/3rd, the deduction cannot be the same if the deceased is survived by a sole dependent.

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench in MFA No.5465 of 2016 in case of The Manager, National Insurance Co Ltd., V/s T.Chandranaika and others wherein the Hon'ble High Court has held in its judgment at para 9 as under:
This view is supported by the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation(2009) 6 SCC 121.

sentences.text:
The relevant paragraphs of the said judgment reads as under:
"30.

Though in some cases the deduction to be made towards personal and living expenses is calculated on the basis of units indicated in Trilok Chandra, the general practice is to apply standardized deductions.

Having considered several subsequent decisions of this court, we are of the view that where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, should be one-third (1/3rd) where the number of dependent family members 2 to 3, one- fourth(1/4th) where the number of dependent family members is 4 to 6, and one-fifty (1/5th) where the number of dependent family members exceeds six.
This implies that when there is only one dependent of the deceased, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be taken as 1/2."
This Tribunal carefully perused the above judgments of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
The ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka is aptly applicable to the case on hand as in the case on hand there is only one dependent of deceased.
So, in view of the above reported judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of deceased is considered 1/2.

20. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondent No.1 & 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Goods Tempo bearing Regn.No.KA-53-D-0828 by its driver.
There appears to be no dispute related to ownership of respondent No.1 pertaining to the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 is the insurer of offending vehicle.

The materials on record disclose that the offending vehicle was having valid and effective policy of insurance and the driver of offending vehicle was having valid and effective licence as on the date of accident.
So, the respondent No.1 and 2, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of .25,21,854/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs Twenty One Thousand Eight Hundred and Fifty Four only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank and the remaining 60% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of Bank Account of petitioners,
with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.

opennyai_summary.issue:
6. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.
Whether petitioner proves that the son of petitioner namely Manjunatha N.M.,
succumbed to the injuries in the accident that took place on 10.07.2022 at about 07.30 p.m., near Uratiagrahara Gate, H.Cross, Chintamani Road, Kolar Taluk and District, when he was riding a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-67-H- 3822, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Goods Tempo bearing Regn.No.KA-53-D-0828 by its driver?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
4. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
But the driver of offending vehicle has not been examined before the tribunal by the respondents.
The IMV Report furnished before the tribunal clearly discloses the aspect of damages caused to the vehicle and no explanation is forthcoming regarding manner of damages caused to the vehicle.
The said aspect indicates involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
If the vehicle was not involved in the accident, then the respondent No.1 could have explained the manner of damage caused to the vehicle either to I.O or before the tribunal.
But respondent No.1 not provided any explanation in that regard in the objections filed by him.
Further, respondent No.1 could have stated before the I.O regarding non- involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
Respondent No.1 stated in the objection regarding the notice issued by I.O and getting the vehicle released by furnishing the documents.
On the said occasion, respondent No.1 could have stated that the vehicle was not involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of driver in the cause of accident.
But, the respondent No.1 does not appear to have stated anything about the non-involvement of the vehicle before the police.
Mere non-mentioning of registration number of the vehicle cannot be considered to be sufficient and satisfactory proof to doubt the involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
But, no satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to substantiate the said contention.
The materials on record do not disclose the aspect of implicating the offending vehicle in the case.
In the cross examination of PW.1 also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited from the witness.
16. The respondents not placed sufficient and satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
The materials on record disclose the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The materials on record do not disclose the aspect of implication of offending vehicle in the case and not sufficient to substantiate the contention of respondents.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the documents furnished by the petitioners are to be looked into in order to ascertain the aspect of negligence.
So, the oral and documentary evidence placed by the petitioners discloses that the accident was caused due to rash and negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
As per the materials placed by the petitioners, the age of deceased appears to be 30 years as on the date of accident.
The respondents not furnished any materials to rebut or disprove the documents furnished by petitioners related to age of deceased.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the documents furnished by petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the age of deceased.
As per the materials, the age of the deceased is 30 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration.
The materials placed by the petitioners are not sufficient and satisfactory to show the occupation and income of the deceased.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional income is to be taken into consideration.
By considering the facts and circumstances of case, the notional income of deceased is considered as .15,500/- per month.
In Hem Raj V/s
the Oriental Insurance Company Ltd and others
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench in MFA No.5465 of 2016 in case of The Manager, National Insurance Co Ltd., V/s T.Chandranaika and others wherein the Hon'ble High Court has held in its judgment at para 9 as under:
This view is supported by the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation(2009) 6 SCC 121.
So, in view of ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Pranay Sethi case, the petitioner is entitled for additional 10% on conventional heads which is to be enhanced on percentage basis in every three years and the enhancement should be at the rate of 10% in a span of three years.

21. Issue No.3:
In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of .25,21,854/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs Twenty One Thousand Eight Hundred and Fifty Four only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank and the remaining 60% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.
The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of Bank Account of petitioners,
with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to their account after expiry of three years period of deposit, without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
